Subject: Service boundary termination & DNS steering ownership

Hi Aditya / Marissa,

We're getting ready to onboard Redwood into our VPC (Fintegral production account) and need firm answers on two operational items before we sign off on the infra ticket:

1) Where should TLS terminate for private endpoints in our topology? We have an ALB -> NLB -> customer ingress gateway pattern, and we'd like to understand the recommended default (customer terminates vs Redwood-managed inside our VPC) and the tradeoffs.

2) DNS steering and ownership: who is expected to control authoritative records vs. who manages health-based failover or internal service mapping? We need this called out clearly for our networking team and procurement.

Attached: Network-Diagram-v1.png, Fintegral-Security-Profile.pdf (security checklist).

Can you provide a short responsibility matrix and a proposed rotation cadence for certs (we use AWS KMS/HSM today)? Also propose a 30-min window for a quick alignment call.

Subject: Re: Service boundary termination & DNS steering ownership

Alice — thanks for the clear ask and the diagram. I outlined the options below and a suggested default for faster time-to-production. I attached a one-page ownership matrix (redwood-ownership-matrix.csv) you can drop into your runbook.

Short recommendation (default): Customer terminates TLS at ingress (ALB/NLB) and presents an internal trusted cert to downstream services. Why: gives Fintegral full control over keys, aligns with zero-trust posture, and avoids cross-account key escrow. This is our preferred pattern when customers have KMS/HSM and can automate rotation.

Alternative (when customer cannot manage TLS rotation): Redwood terminates inside the VPC on a private sidecar/edge instance we operate (we can deploy an inference proxy in your account with delegated cert lifecycle). Pros: simpler for customers, Redwood handles OCSP/CRL/renewal; Cons: requires delegated trust (short-lived certs + strict audit).

DNS steering responsibilities (suggested):
- Fintegral (customer): authoritative public/private zone ownership, A/ALIAS for ingress, zone SOA and TTL control.
- Redwood: health check endpoints, internal resolver mappings for service fallback, SRV/weighted routing metadata for canaries. Redwood will not modify authoritative records unless explicitly delegated by change control.

Cert rotation & key management (suggested cadence):
- Customer-managed: 90-day cert TTL recommended, automated rotation via KMS/HSM + ACME hook or internal CA. Customer provides CSR or accepts short-lived certs (recommended).
- Redwood-managed: automatic rotation, 30–60 day TTL for workload certs, integration with customer's KMS via AWS KMS grants or HSM proxy.

Operational asks from Fintegral for the preferred default (customer-terminates or Redwood-sidecar), a staging VPC CIDR and an IAM role for Redwood deploys (if choosing Redwood-sidecar).

Next steps: I attached the ownership matrix (redwood-ownership-matrix.csv). Can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow? I have 11–11:30am PT and 3–3:30pm PT open.

Attachments: redwood-ownership-matrix.csv (text/csv)

On Fri, Sep 25, 2026 at 10:05 AM Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com> wrote:
> Short recommendation (default): Customer terminates TLS at ingress (ALB/NLB) and presents an internal trusted cert to downstream services.

Hi Alice — quick operational additions from SRE/security perspective:
- Require OCSP stapling or short-lived certs for any path that terminates at our sidecars. We will reject long-lived certs without stapling in production.
- CRL/OCSP expectations need to be documented in the runbook (we can include template checks).
- Rotation cadence: agree on 90-day for customer-managed public-facing certs, but recommend 30–60 day for workload certs if Redwood is managing.

Phased rollout recommendation:
1) Staging: non-prod environment, 48-hour monitoring window for tokenized traffic.
2) Canary: 2% traffic for 24 hours, validate latency and error budget.
3) Full: ramp to 100% with rollback window and rollback playbook attached to the runbook doc.

I've linked a draft mutual action plan here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A2B3C-mutual-action-plan — please add your security runbook items.

Can Kimberly and Aditya include the SRE owner for the canary checks? Alice — what windows do your network ops team have for staged DNS changes (we prefer a UTC midnight–02:00 maintenance window for low global impact).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
